$comment: Shape grammar — the rule lives in docs/adr/0003-shape-grammar.md. A shape encodes the NATURE of an object, never its importance nor its state. Nine shapes, no more.

application.label: Application
application.nature: something a person interacts with directly

stream.label: Stream
stream.nature: a queue, a topic, a bus — data passing through

actor.label: Actor
actor.nature: a person, or the workstation they act through
actor.geometry: rounded rectangle on a light grey fill

device.label: Device
device.nature: a physical device outside the information system

external.label: External
external.geometry: rounded rectangle, dashed stroke, grey fill

boundary.label: Boundary
boundary.nature: a zone: network, trust, deployment, context
boundary.remark: a container, not a node: no arrow ever connects to it

node.label: Deployment node
node.nature: a machine that hosts: physical server, virtual machine, cluster node
node.geometry: square-cornered rectangle, thick stroke, very light grey fill

ruledOut.diamond: reserved for flowcharts — a decision has no place in an architecture view
ruledOut.cloud: ambiguous: “the internet”, “a cloud provider” or “I don't know”, depending on the reader; use “external”
ruledOut.hexagon: no established meaning; competes with the capsule without adding anything
